quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Climate scientists analyzing several decades of data from a mountain research station found that the elevation at which a particular alpine wildflower species blooms each spring has shifted upward by roughly two hundred meters compared to where it typically bloomed forty years ago, a change that correlates closely with rising average spring temperatures recorded at the same station, though the researchers noted that pollinator insect populations at the new, higher elevation have not shifted upward at nearly the same pace.
options: Pollinator insects have shifted upward faster than the wildflower species.
Both the wildflower and its pollinators have shifted at an identical pace.
Rising temperatures have had no measurable effect on where the wildflower blooms.
The wildflower's shift to higher elevations may be outpacing the movement of the insects that pollinate it.
quests.correctAnswer: The wildflower's shift to higher elevations may be outpacing the movement of the insects that pollinate it.
quests.hint: Compare how much the wildflower's blooming elevation has shifted with how much the pollinator population has shifted.
quests.explanation: The wildflower has moved upslope by two hundred meters while its pollinators haven't kept pace, suggesting a growing mismatch between where the flowers now bloom and where the insects that pollinate them are found.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A multinational company that allowed regional offices to set their own policies on remote work, rather than mandating a single company-wide rule, found substantial variation in productivity outcomes across offices: offices that combined remote flexibility with clearly defined core collaboration hours, during which all team members were expected to be reachable, reported productivity gains, while offices that offered flexibility without any defined core hours reported a slight decline in project completion speed over the same period.
options: Remote work flexibility appears to benefit productivity mainly when paired with defined core collaboration hours.
Remote work flexibility improved productivity regardless of whether core hours were defined.
Defined core hours alone, without remote flexibility, produced the best outcomes.
Every regional office reported identical productivity outcomes under the new policy.
quests.correctAnswer: Remote work flexibility appears to benefit productivity mainly when paired with defined core collaboration hours.
quests.hint: Compare the two types of offices, noting what distinguished the ones with productivity gains from the ones with declines.
quests.explanation: Only offices that paired flexibility with defined core hours saw productivity gains, while offices without core hours saw a decline, suggesting the flexibility itself wasn't enough without some structure to keep teams coordinated.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A researcher studying multigenerational households, where grandparents live with their adult children and grandchildren under one roof, found that households where grandparents took on a clearly defined role, such as being primarily responsible for after-school childcare, reported higher overall family satisfaction than households where grandparents lived in the home but had no specific defined responsibilities, with family members in the latter group frequently describing role confusion and occasional friction over decision-making authority.
options: Households without defined grandparent roles reported the highest satisfaction.
Grandparents having a clearly defined role appears linked to greater satisfaction in multigenerational households.
The presence or absence of a defined role made no difference to family satisfaction.
Role confusion was equally common in both types of households.
quests.correctAnswer: Grandparents having a clearly defined role appears linked to greater satisfaction in multigenerational households.
quests.hint: Compare satisfaction levels between households where the grandparent's role was clearly defined and those where it wasn't.
quests.explanation: Households with a clearly defined role for grandparents reported higher satisfaction than those without one, where confusion and friction were more common, suggesting clarity about responsibilities helps multigenerational households function more smoothly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional airport authority that operates three smaller airports within the same metropolitan area found that after consolidating all rental car counters into a single shared facility connected to all three airports by shuttle, rather than each airport maintaining its own separate counters, overall rental car wait times increased for travelers at the two smaller airports, even though total operating costs for the rental car companies decreased significantly across the entire region, according to a report commissioned the following year.
options: Consolidation reduced both costs and wait times for all travelers.
Wait times decreased at the two smaller airports after consolidation.
Consolidation had no effect on either costs or wait times.
Consolidating rental car counters appears to have reduced costs at the expense of convenience for some travelers.
quests.correctAnswer: Consolidating rental car counters appears to have reduced costs at the expense of convenience for some travelers.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes a benefit for the rental car companies alongside a drawback for some travelers.
quests.explanation: Costs dropped for rental car companies after consolidation, but wait times rose for travelers at the smaller airports, suggesting the efficiency gained from a shared facility came at the cost of convenience for some passengers.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A cybersecurity firm that studied phishing email susceptibility across several large companies found that employees who had completed a single mandatory training session a year earlier were no less likely to click on a simulated phishing link than employees who had never completed any training at all, but employees who received brief, randomized simulated phishing tests every few months, with immediate feedback after each one, showed a substantial and lasting improvement over the two-year study period.
options: A single annual training session was highly effective at preventing phishing clicks.
Ongoing practice with immediate feedback appears far more effective at preventing phishing clicks than a single training session.
Neither training approach had any measurable effect on phishing susceptibility.
Employees with no training at all performed best in the study.
quests.correctAnswer: Ongoing practice with immediate feedback appears far more effective at preventing phishing clicks than a single training session.
quests.hint: Compare the effectiveness of the one-time training with the effectiveness of ongoing simulated tests.
quests.explanation: A single training session showed no real improvement, while ongoing simulated tests with immediate feedback produced a lasting improvement, suggesting that repeated practice, not a one-time session, is what actually changes behavior around phishing emails.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university that had always required all incoming international students to complete the same standardized six-week orientation program, regardless of their country of origin or prior study-abroad experience, began offering an abbreviated two-week version for students who had already studied in an English-speaking country for at least one full academic year. Academic performance during the first semester was statistically similar between students who completed the full orientation and those who completed the abbreviated version, provided they had the qualifying prior experience.
options: The abbreviated orientation led to significantly worse academic performance.
For students with relevant prior experience, the abbreviated orientation appears just as effective as the full program.
All students, regardless of prior experience, performed better with the full orientation.
The length of orientation had no bearing on any student's academic performance.
quests.correctAnswer: For students with relevant prior experience, the abbreviated orientation appears just as effective as the full program.
quests.hint: Notice the passage specifies which students were eligible for the abbreviated version.
quests.explanation: Students with qualifying prior experience performed similarly whether they completed the full or abbreviated orientation, suggesting that for that specific group, the shorter version provided sufficient preparation without requiring the full six weeks.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional hospital system that introduced a policy requiring a mandatory ten-minute cooling-off period before any elective but non-urgent second opinion could be scheduled found that patients who went through the waiting period were slightly less likely to ultimately pursue an unnecessary duplicate procedure, based on a review of insurance claims, though patient satisfaction surveys showed a modest decline among patients who felt the waiting period was patronizing or unnecessary given their own research into their condition.
options: The waiting period increased both unnecessary procedures and patient satisfaction.
Patient satisfaction improved significantly because of the waiting period.
The waiting period had no measurable effect on procedures or satisfaction.
The waiting period appears to have reduced unnecessary procedures while slightly lowering some patients' satisfaction.
quests.correctAnswer: The waiting period appears to have reduced unnecessary procedures while slightly lowering some patients' satisfaction.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions one outcome that improved and one that declined.
quests.explanation: Unnecessary duplicate procedures decreased under the waiting period, but some patients felt the requirement was patronizing, showing the policy achieved its clinical goal at some cost to how certain patients experienced their care.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city council debating whether to approve a large mixed-use development downtown reviewed economic impact studies from three comparable cities that had approved similar projects in the past decade. In each case, retail vacancy rates in the surrounding blocks dropped within two years of the new development opening, but rental prices for existing nearby apartments also rose noticeably faster than the citywide average during that same two-year period, a pattern each of the three studies noted independently despite covering different cities.
options: The developments reduced both retail vacancy and nearby rent increases.
Downtown development projects like this one may reduce retail vacancy while also accelerating nearby rent increases.
Rental prices near the developments rose more slowly than the citywide average.
The developments had no measurable effect on either vacancy rates or rents.
quests.correctAnswer: Downtown development projects like this one may reduce retail vacancy while also accelerating nearby rent increases.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes two different trends that occurred together in each of the three cities.
quests.explanation: Retail vacancy fell and nearby rents rose faster than average in all three comparable cities, suggesting this specific type of downtown development tends to come with both a commercial benefit and a housing cost trade-off.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An analysis comparing two employer-sponsored retirement plan designs found that plans defaulting new employees into a diversified target-date fund, rather than requiring employees to actively choose investments from a long list of options, resulted in far fewer employees holding an overly conservative all-cash allocation years into their careers, a pattern researchers had previously linked, in earlier interviews, to employees simply avoiding an overwhelming decision rather than making any deliberate investment choice at all.
options: Requiring employees to actively choose investments led to more diversified portfolios.
Both plan designs resulted in identical investment allocations over time.
Defaulting employees into a diversified fund appears to prevent the kind of accidental over-caution that comes from decision avoidance.
Employees who avoided the decision entirely ended up with the most diversified portfolios.
quests.correctAnswer: Defaulting employees into a diversified fund appears to prevent the kind of accidental over-caution that comes from decision avoidance.
quests.hint: Think about what an overly conservative all-cash allocation years later suggests about how the original decision was made.
quests.explanation: Employees defaulted into a diversified fund were far less likely to end up holding an all-cash allocation than those who had to choose, suggesting the default helped avoid the passive, avoidance-driven conservatism seen under the choice-based design.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A state environmental agency comparing two approaches to reducing highway litter, roadside signs threatening fines versus a program adopting stretches of highway under a local business's name displayed on a sign, found that the adopt-a-highway program resulted in measurably less litter accumulation over a five-year period, even in stretches where the threatened fines were rarely if ever actually enforced by state troopers patrolling the area, according to the agency's five-year cleanup and litter-count records.
options: Threatened fines were more effective than the adoption program at reducing litter.
Enforcement of fines was consistently high in both types of highway stretches.
A sense of local ownership through the adoption program appears more effective than an unenforced threat of fines.
Neither approach had any measurable effect on litter accumulation.
quests.correctAnswer: A sense of local ownership through the adoption program appears more effective than an unenforced threat of fines.
quests.hint: Notice that the fines were rarely enforced, yet one approach still worked better.
quests.explanation: The adoption program reduced litter more than the fine-based signs, even where fines went largely unenforced, suggesting that a sense of local ownership or visible accountability may motivate behavior more than a threat that isn't actually carried out.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A food science team testing consumer response to plant-based meat alternatives found that participants who were told a product's ingredient list before tasting it rated the taste significantly lower, on average, than participants who tasted the identical product without seeing the ingredient list first, even though every participant in the study rated the same physical sample prepared from the exact same batch of product on the exact same day, according to the study's blind-tasting protocol.
options: Seeing the ingredient list improved how participants rated the taste.
The ingredient list had no bearing on participants' taste ratings.
Knowing the ingredients in advance appears to lower how people perceive the taste of a food, independent of the food itself.
Participants tasted physically different samples depending on the group they were in.
quests.correctAnswer: Knowing the ingredients in advance appears to lower how people perceive the taste of a food, independent of the food itself.
quests.hint: Notice that the food itself was identical for both groups; only what participants knew in advance differed.
quests.explanation: Participants who saw the ingredient list first rated the same food lower than those who didn't, suggesting that expectations formed before tasting can shape perceived taste even when the food itself hasn't changed at all.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A sports psychologist working with a college volleyball team introduced a brief, structured pre-game visualization routine, asking players to mentally rehearse specific in-game scenarios for five minutes before each match. Over a full season, the team's performance in high-pressure situations, such as close final sets, improved measurably compared to the previous season, although the team's overall win-loss record remained roughly the same as the year before, since the team also faced a notably tougher schedule of opponents that season, according to the coaching staff.
options: The team's overall win-loss record improved dramatically because of the routine.
The visualization routine had no measurable effect on the team's performance.
The visualization routine appears to have improved performance specifically in high-pressure moments, even though the overall record didn't change much.
High-pressure performance declined after the visualization routine was introduced.
quests.correctAnswer: The visualization routine appears to have improved performance specifically in high-pressure moments, even though the overall record didn't change much.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates high-pressure performance from the team's overall season record.
quests.explanation: High-pressure performance improved even though the overall record stayed similar, and the passage notes the team faced tougher opponents that year, suggesting the routine had a real, specific effect that a simple win-loss count wouldn't fully capture.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city's public art commission that had always selected sculptures for a riverfront park through a closed panel of art experts began including an online public vote as thirty percent of the final selection score, with expert judges retaining the remaining seventy percent. The pieces ultimately selected under the new hybrid system attracted noticeably more foot traffic and social media attention than pieces selected purely by the expert panel in previous years, though several art critics complained the new selections favored crowd-pleasing over artistically ambitious work.
options: The hybrid system increased public engagement with no complaints from critics.
The hybrid selection system appears to have increased public engagement, though possibly at some cost to artistic ambition.
Foot traffic and social media attention declined under the new system.
Art critics were uniformly pleased with the pieces selected under the new system.
quests.correctAnswer: The hybrid selection system appears to have increased public engagement, though possibly at some cost to artistic ambition.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions both a popular success and a critical concern about the new system.
quests.explanation: Public engagement rose under the hybrid system, but some critics felt the selections became less artistically ambitious, suggesting the change succeeded at broadening appeal while raising a real trade-off about artistic risk-taking.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A consulting firm that tracked which junior employees were promoted to senior roles within five years found that junior employees who were assigned to at least one project outside their primary specialty during their first two years were promoted at meaningfully higher rates than junior employees who worked exclusively within their original specialty, even after the firm's analysts statistically accounted for differences in performance review scores between the two groups of employees.
options: Cross-specialty project experience early in a career seems linked to higher promotion rates beyond what performance scores alone explain.
Staying within one's original specialty led to higher promotion rates.
Performance review scores fully explained the difference in promotion rates.
Promotion rates were identical regardless of project assignment history.
quests.correctAnswer: Cross-specialty project experience early in a career seems linked to higher promotion rates beyond what performance scores alone explain.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions that performance scores were accounted for separately from the promotion pattern.
quests.explanation: Employees with cross-specialty project experience were promoted more often, even after accounting for performance scores, suggesting the broader experience itself, not just how well someone performed, played a role in advancement.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying video call fatigue among remote workers found that participants who kept their own video feed hidden from their own view during calls, while still being visible to others, reported significantly less end-of-day tiredness than participants who could see their own live video feed throughout each call, even though both groups spent an identical number of hours in video meetings each day, based on daily fatigue surveys collected over a four-week period from several hundred participants.
options: Hiding one's own video feed increased end-of-day tiredness.
The number of meeting hours was the only factor affecting fatigue.
Seeing one's own video feed during calls appears to contribute to fatigue, separate from the number of hours spent in meetings.
Fatigue levels were identical regardless of whether participants saw their own feed.
quests.correctAnswer: Seeing one's own video feed during calls appears to contribute to fatigue, separate from the number of hours spent in meetings.
quests.hint: Notice that meeting hours were equal between groups; only the self-view setting differed.
quests.explanation: Participants who hid their own video feed reported less fatigue than those who could see themselves, even with identical meeting hours, suggesting that watching oneself on camera, not just the meetings themselves, contributes to video call fatigue.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A researcher studying adult siblings who had experienced their parents' divorce during childhood found that siblings who had been encouraged by at least one parent to maintain their own individual relationship with the other parent, rather than being asked to take sides, reported closer relationships with each other as adults than siblings who described feeling pressured to align with one parent over the other during the divorce process itself, based on interviews with adult sibling pairs from several dozen divorced families.
options: Feeling pressured to take sides led to closer adult sibling relationships.
How children were treated during a divorce had no bearing on adult sibling relationships.
Every sibling pair in the study reported identical relationship quality as adults.
Being allowed to maintain an independent relationship with each parent appears linked to closer adult sibling relationships.
quests.correctAnswer: Being allowed to maintain an independent relationship with each parent appears linked to closer adult sibling relationships.
quests.hint: Compare the two groups of siblings based on how they were treated during their parents' divorce.
quests.explanation: Siblings who weren't pressured to take sides reported closer relationships with each other as adults, suggesting that being freed from divided loyalty during a difficult time may have protected their bond with each other.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A physical therapy clinic that switched from scheduling all patients in fixed thirty-minute slots to a flexible scheduling system, where session length varied based on the complexity of each patient's treatment plan, found that patient-reported outcomes improved modestly overall, but therapists reported that the clinic's total daily patient capacity dropped by roughly fifteen percent, since more complex cases now occupied longer blocks of time than the old fixed schedule had allowed for any single patient.
options: Flexible session lengths appear to have improved outcomes for patients while reducing how many patients the clinic could see each day.
Flexible scheduling improved outcomes without affecting how many patients could be seen.
Patient capacity increased under the flexible scheduling system.
Session length had no bearing on patient outcomes or clinic capacity.
quests.correctAnswer: Flexible session lengths appear to have improved outcomes for patients while reducing how many patients the clinic could see each day.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions a benefit for patients alongside a cost for the clinic's overall capacity.
quests.explanation: Patient outcomes improved modestly under flexible scheduling, but the clinic's daily capacity dropped because complex cases took longer, suggesting the more personalized approach came with a real trade-off in how many patients could be treated each day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A mattress retailer that had always offered only a thirty-day return window found that extending the window to one hundred days led to a modest increase in returns overall, but also led to a substantial increase in initial sales, since customer surveys showed the longer window meaningfully reduced the perceived risk of purchasing an expensive item that customers could not physically test for an extended period at home before deciding whether to keep it.
options: The longer return window reduced both sales and returns.
Returns increased so much that overall sales declined.
The length of the return window had no bearing on either sales or returns.
The longer return window appears to have boosted sales more than it increased returns, likely by reducing perceived purchase risk.
quests.correctAnswer: The longer return window appears to have boosted sales more than it increased returns, likely by reducing perceived purchase risk.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes the return window's effect on two separate outcomes: sales and returns.
quests.explanation: Sales rose substantially while returns rose only modestly after the window was extended, suggesting that reducing customers' perceived risk in trying the mattress at home was worth more to sales than the small increase in returns cost the retailer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Marine biologists tracking a population of sea turtles that nest on a protected beach found that turtles fitted with small, lightweight satellite tags showed nesting success rates statistically indistinguishable from untagged turtles nesting on the same beach, addressing earlier concerns among some conservationists that the tagging process itself might interfere with a turtle's willingness or ability to nest successfully in subsequent seasons, a concern the research team specifically designed the multi-year study to investigate.
options: Tagged turtles showed significantly lower nesting success than untagged turtles.
Tagging improved nesting success compared to untagged turtles.
The study found no way to compare tagged and untagged turtles' nesting success.
The tagging process does not appear to interfere with turtles' nesting success.
quests.correctAnswer: The tagging process does not appear to interfere with turtles' nesting success.
quests.hint: Compare nesting success rates between tagged and untagged turtles.
quests.explanation: Tagged and untagged turtles showed similar nesting success rates, addressing the concern that tagging might interfere with nesting, and suggesting the tags themselves were not harming the turtles' reproductive behavior.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A budget airline that eliminated seat-back pockets from its aircraft, citing weight reduction and fuel savings, found that the change reduced average fuel costs per flight by a small but measurable amount, but customer complaint volume related to 'nowhere to put my phone or headphones' rose noticeably in the months following the change, eventually prompting the airline to install a simple elastic strap in place of the removed pockets on all affected aircraft.
options: Removing the pockets increased fuel costs and reduced complaints.
Passengers had no complaints related to the removal of seat-back pockets.
Removing the seat-back pockets saved fuel costs but created a new source of passenger frustration.
The airline reversed the change entirely and reinstalled the original pockets.
quests.correctAnswer: Removing the seat-back pockets saved fuel costs but created a new source of passenger frustration.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes a benefit for the airline and a drawback for passengers.
quests.explanation: Fuel costs dropped after the pockets were removed, but passenger complaints rose, showing the change achieved its cost-saving goal while creating a real inconvenience that the airline eventually had to partially address.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A high school that switched its foreign language requirement from two years of a single language to allowing students to split their two required years between two different languages found that students who split their requirement reported enjoying the courses more, according to end-of-year surveys, but standardized proficiency test scores in either language were noticeably lower than scores among students who had completed two full years in a single language, based on results from the district's spring exam.
options: Splitting language study across two languages appears to increase enjoyment but reduce measurable proficiency in either one.
Splitting language study increased both enjoyment and proficiency scores.
Proficiency scores were identical regardless of how students split their language study.
Students who split their requirement reported enjoying the courses less.
quests.correctAnswer: Splitting language study across two languages appears to increase enjoyment but reduce measurable proficiency in either one.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates how much students enjoyed the courses from how well they performed on proficiency tests.
quests.explanation: Students who split their language requirement enjoyed it more but scored lower on proficiency tests than students who focused on one language, suggesting the trade-off was between enjoyment and measurable skill depth in either language.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional orchestra that had always performed the same core repertoire of well-known classical works experimented with devoting one concert per season entirely to commissioned pieces by living composers. Attendance at the new-music concerts was consistently lower than attendance at traditional programming, but subscriber retention, the percentage of season ticket holders who renewed the following year, was highest among subscribers who had attended at least one new-music concert during the season, according to renewal records reviewed over three consecutive seasons.
options: New-music concerts drew larger audiences than traditional programming.
New-music concerts appear to draw smaller audiences but may strengthen loyalty among subscribers who attend them.
Subscriber retention was lowest among those who attended new-music concerts.
New-music concerts had no measurable effect on attendance or subscriber retention.
quests.correctAnswer: New-music concerts appear to draw smaller audiences but may strengthen loyalty among subscribers who attend them.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates attendance at a single concert from overall subscriber renewal behavior.
quests.explanation: New-music concerts drew smaller crowds, but subscribers who attended them renewed at the highest rates, suggesting that while these concerts aren't broadly popular, they may deepen commitment among the subscribers who do attend.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city that had always funded its public parks through general tax revenue considered switching a portion of park funding to a system of small user fees for specific amenities, such as reserving a picnic pavilion or sports field. Public feedback sessions revealed strong support for fees on reservable amenities used by a minority of residents, but strong opposition to any fee for basic access to trails, playgrounds, or open green space used regularly by the broader community.
options: Residents supported fees equally across all types of park amenities.
Residents opposed all forms of park fees without exception.
Public feedback showed no clear pattern in support for or against fees.
Residents appear to distinguish between amenities used by a few and basic access used by many when it comes to fees.
quests.correctAnswer: Residents appear to distinguish between amenities used by a few and basic access used by many when it comes to fees.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates residents' views on reservable amenities from their views on basic open access.
quests.explanation: Residents supported fees for amenities like reservable pavilions but opposed fees for basic access like trails and playgrounds, suggesting a distinction in public opinion based on how exclusively an amenity is used versus how broadly it serves the community.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional bank that began offering a round-up savings feature, automatically rounding up debit card purchases to the nearest dollar and depositing the difference into savings, found that customers using the feature saved modestly more per month on average than customers who did not use it, but a follow-up survey found that many round-up users had not noticed or adjusted their regular spending habits at all, crediting the small, painless increments for the extra savings rather than any deliberate budgeting effort.
options: Customers using the feature made significant deliberate changes to their spending habits.
The round-up feature had no measurable effect on how much customers saved.
The round-up feature appears to increase savings through small, unnoticed increments rather than through deliberate budgeting changes.
Customers who did not use the feature saved more on average.
quests.correctAnswer: The round-up feature appears to increase savings through small, unnoticed increments rather than through deliberate budgeting changes.
quests.hint: Notice what the follow-up survey revealed about how users perceived their own savings.
quests.explanation: Round-up users saved more without noticing changes in their spending, suggesting the extra savings came from small automatic increments rather than any conscious budgeting decision on the customer's part.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team analyzing usage of a home energy monitoring app found that households that received a single push notification per week, summarizing their energy use compared to the previous week, reduced consumption by a modest amount over six months, but households that received a daily notification with the same type of comparison actually reduced consumption less than the weekly-notification group, a result the team attributed to users eventually ignoring or muting notifications that arrived too frequently.
options: Daily notifications were more effective than weekly ones at reducing consumption.
Weekly notifications appear to have been more effective than daily ones, possibly because daily alerts became easy to ignore.
Both notification frequencies produced identical reductions in consumption.
Notification frequency had no bearing on how much households reduced their energy use.
quests.correctAnswer: Weekly notifications appear to have been more effective than daily ones, possibly because daily alerts became easy to ignore.
quests.hint: Compare the two notification frequencies, and consider the explanation the team offers for the difference.
quests.explanation: Weekly notifications led to greater reductions in energy use than daily ones, and the researchers suggest this happened because more frequent alerts became easy for users to tune out, reducing their overall impact over time.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A youth swim league that switched from awarding medals to only the top three finishers in each race to awarding a personal-best ribbon to any swimmer who beat their own previous time, regardless of finishing place, found that overall participation in swim meets increased the following season, particularly among swimmers who had rarely finished in the top three under the old medal system and had previously skipped a number of optional meets earlier in their swimming careers.
options: Rewarding personal improvement rather than only placement appears to have specifically boosted participation among swimmers who rarely medaled before.
Participation declined most among swimmers who rarely finished in the top three.
The change in awards had no measurable effect on meet participation.
Only the league's top swimmers increased their meet participation.
quests.correctAnswer: Rewarding personal improvement rather than only placement appears to have specifically boosted participation among swimmers who rarely medaled before.
quests.hint: Notice which specific group of swimmers showed the biggest increase in participation.
quests.explanation: Participation rose most among swimmers who had rarely medaled before, suggesting that recognizing personal improvement, not just finishing place, gave a wider range of swimmers a reason to keep competing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large coffee chain that tested replacing single-use plastic straws with paper straws at half of its locations, while keeping plastic straws at the other half as a comparison group, found that customer complaints about straws rose noticeably at paper-straw locations, primarily related to the straws becoming soggy in cold drinks, but a customer survey found that a majority of respondents still said they supported the switch for environmental reasons despite the practical complaints they had raised.
options: Customers appear to have accepted the paper straws' practical downsides because they valued the environmental trade-off.
Customers rejected the environmental reasoning behind the switch to paper straws.
Complaints about straws decreased at the paper-straw locations.
Customer opinions were identical regarding both types of straws.
quests.correctAnswer: Customers appear to have accepted the paper straws' practical downsides because they valued the environmental trade-off.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates practical complaints from customers' broader opinion about the switch.
quests.explanation: Complaints about paper straws rose, yet most customers still said they supported the switch for environmental reasons, suggesting people were willing to tolerate a practical downside in service of a goal they valued more.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A large hospital network that surveyed nurses about scheduling preferences before implementing self-scheduling software, which allowed nurses to select and trade shifts among themselves within certain guardrails rather than having a manager build the schedule manually, found that nurse-reported job satisfaction increased significantly in the first year, though the network's scheduling administrators reported that a small number of less popular overnight and holiday shifts became noticeably harder to fill without direct managerial assignment.
options: Self-scheduling appears to have improved nurse satisfaction while creating a new challenge in filling unpopular shifts.
Self-scheduling improved satisfaction with no new challenges for administrators.
Nurse satisfaction declined after self-scheduling was introduced.
Filling unpopular shifts became easier under the new self-scheduling system.
quests.correctAnswer: Self-scheduling appears to have improved nurse satisfaction while creating a new challenge in filling unpopular shifts.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions a benefit for nurses alongside a new difficulty for administrators.
quests.explanation: Nurse satisfaction rose under self-scheduling, but unpopular shifts became harder to fill without direct assignment, suggesting the added autonomy came with a real administrative trade-off around covering less desirable shifts.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A coastal city comparing two seawall designs to protect against rising tides, a traditional solid concrete wall and a newer design incorporating gaps that allow limited water flow while still blocking major surges, found that the gapped design better preserved nearby tidal marsh ecosystems over a five-year monitoring period, though engineers noted the gapped design required more frequent inspection and maintenance than the simpler solid concrete wall, according to a joint report from the city's engineering and environmental departments.
options: The gapped seawall design appears to better protect ecosystems at the cost of requiring more upkeep.
The solid concrete wall better preserved the tidal marsh ecosystems.
The gapped design required less maintenance than the solid wall.
Neither seawall design had any measurable effect on the marsh ecosystems.
